transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, September 15. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. On Amit Shah's UCC implementation claim, 3 BJP allies sound caution. No Talks On This So Far: TDP; LJP For Transparency 'Are they living in the past?': Ex-India cricketer slams Mohsin Naqvi. The celebration of India's Women's Asia Cup triumph was overshadowed when the team rejected the trophy presented by ACC president Mohsin Naqvi. This decision recalls a similar controversy during the men's Asia Cup final. Mohammad Kaif has voiced doubts regarding Naqvi's involvement in both political and sports spheres, reflecting wider issues related to his dual authority in the cricketing community. Oracle layoffs: Employees receive '6am job cuts' email from Oracle leadership again. Oracle layoffs began again on September 14, with employees across the US reporting the same 6am email from "Oracle Leadership" that landed in March. Logins were disabled around 4am, Slack access dropped by 5.30am, and Slack counts fell by 3,000 to 4,000. OCI, Fusion, NetSuite, Oracle Health and the Abilene Stargate site were hit. India's Development Centre is expected next, as Oracle's restructuring bill climbs to $2.8 billion. BJP single-largest party in Rajasthan urban polls, denied sweep by Independents. The recent urban local body elections in Rajasthan showcased the significant influence of independent candidates on the outcome. Although the BJP secured the most seats, they did not dominate as expected, while Congress demonstrated resilience by winning important contests in several towns. The strong showing by independents indicates a shift toward local issues rather than party allegiance. Additionally, the announcement of results was hampered by technical glitches in some areas. 'The mistakes I made, I won't make again': Animesh Kujur ready for Asian Games. Animesh Kujur arrives in Aichi-Nagoya with a 10.14 personal best in the 100m and the national 200m record of 20.32. He has gained confidence from international competitions, learned how to manage his body, when to peak and when to reduce the load. With strong Asian competition ahead, including Japan's Shuhei Tada and Soshi Mizukubo, Kujur believes his Asian Championships mistakes will not be repeated and is targeting medals in all three events. Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales sign historic MoU to break away from UK. Leaders from Scotland, Northern Ireland, and Wales signed a pact seeking independence. This historic agreement signals a shift away from Westminster's long-standing control. The first ministers are committed to self-determination for their respective nations. They also aim to strengthen cooperation on economic and energy matters. Retail inflation surges to 8-month high of 4.8 percent in August. NEW DELHI: Retail inflation based on the consumer price index (CPI) hit an eight-month high of 4.8 percent (y-o-y) in Aug from 4.5 percent in July, driven largely by higher food prices, NSO (National Statistics Office) data released Monday showed. US grandpa's $100K treehouse becomes $325K backyard castle. What started as a simple backyard play area vision transformed into a stunning treehouse sanctuary. Priced at $325,000, this remarkable creation boasts a pirate ship and an exciting zipline. Meticulously designed by professional engineers, the treehouse prioritizes safety and the health of the trees. Its multi-tiered layout offers cozy lofts perfect for family bonding and unforgettable gatherings, making it an enduring family attraction filled with wonder and creativity. CBI files FIR in Disha Salian's death case after HC order. NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and formed a special team to probe the death of Disha Salian, two weeks after Bombay HC ordered it to take over the case. Swedish quarry turned opera venue draws 100K visitors each summer. Once a bustling mining site, Dalhalla is now a stunning open-air concert venue nestled in an abandoned Swedish quarry. Renowned for its outstanding natural acoustics discovered in 1991, this breathtaking locale invites performers and audiences alike to bask in the unique ambiance created by limestone walls shaped by an ancient meteorite impact. Annually, it enchants over 100,000 visitors, adding to the charm of the Dalarna region. Atlanta begins next phase to turn Microsoft-donated land to 20,000 housing units. Microsoft donated land in Atlanta for affordable housing initiatives. This donation supports Mayor Andre Dickens' goal of twenty thousand housing units. A community celebration will mark the land donation and future plans. The Quarry Yards property will focus on community development and resident opportunities.

Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations swept across Madhya Pradesh with colourful processions, decorated pandals, clay idols and chants of 'Ganpati Bappa Morya'. First, Trump agreed to a measure that would bar him and his wife from issuing the types of meme coins that they swiftly launched as he prepared to return to the White House for a second time. Now, a pivotal Senate vote on the cryptocurrency bill on Tuesday could mark a watershed moment for the $2.3 trillion market - but it hinges mainly on whether those sign-offs from Trump go far enough.
